holidays.name: National Candy Corn Day
holidays.description: Celebrate the tri-colored, waxy, love-it-or-hate-it candy that shows up in every Halloween bowl. It's a day to nibble the little yellow, orange and white kernels, or to argue about whether they count as candy at all.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, timed to fall the day before Halloween, when candy corn is at peak popularity. Its origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Candy corn was invented in the 1880s by George Renninger of the Wunderle Candy Company in Philadelphia. It was originally sold as 'Chicken Feed'.

holidays.name: National Text Your Ex Day
holidays.description: A cheeky, risk-filled observance that dares you to fire off a message to a former flame. It's a day for nostalgia, closure or regret, depending on how it goes.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's listed on the day before Halloween, when a ghost from your past might reappear.
holidays.funFact: Many people say the 'ghosting' phenomenon fits right in with the spooky season, since a message to an ex is often a message from the past.

holidays.name: National Treat Your Pet Day
holidays.description: A day to spoil your furry, feathered or scaly roommates with extra snacks, toys and cuddles. Pets are a big part of Halloween too, with costumes and treats for them on the way.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's listed on October 30 in holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Pet costumes are a big part of Halloween. Dressing up dogs in particular has become a popular tradition in the days leading up to October 31.
